headline: Comparative genomics traces gain and loss of miRNAs, domains, and duplicated genes
label: Comparative Genomics Lineage Evolution
summary: Lineage-scale genome comparisons now resolve conserved versus lineage-specific components across mammals, carnivorous plants, and land plants.
synthesis: The dominant thread is genome-wide comparative analysis used to track how genetic elements are gained, lost, and diversified across lineages. A homology-plus-synteny framework assigns microRNA orthology across 73 mammalian genomes, outperforming Infernal and MirMachine, and maps family gains and losses. A chromosome-scale Sarracenia purpurea genome, compared with eight angiosperms, links polyploidy-derived regulatory genes and tandem-duplicated ecological genes to convergent innovation. Across 446 genomes spanning major plant lineages, protein domains and domain combinations are traced to separate core from non-core gain and loss. What is new is lineage-scale resolution of conserved versus lineage-specific components. The studies differ in organism and element type and share a comparative genomic framework rather than a single question.
